assessments.closureRisk: Low — no external blocker; closable within one budget unit if variants are materially different.
assessments.dominantCost: Variant construction and re-running causal-episode probes across variants.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Build 2-3 materially different bounded encounter variants, re-run causal-episode probes, separate surviving priors from overfit.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: AF002 priors are partly fixed-encounter overfit; robustness/generalization claims unearned until variants perturb topology/position/resource/target.

assessments.closureRisk: Low but marginal research value is minimal — mostly operational closeout, not new knowledge.
assessments.dominantCost: Final gate execution and structured self-release.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Run final portable and physical gates; commit and graduate if gates pass.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Mechanism selection is complete; only final acceptance/commit/release remain.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Near-complete; another budget unit adds little frontier value beyond a no-op closeout.

assessments.closureRisk: Medium — may resolve to 'no narrower surface justified' (no-op), and dogfooding adds cost.
assessments.dominantCost: Dependency graph audit and packaging candidate construction.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Audit import/dependency graph; build smallest packaging candidate only if measurable; dogfood.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Semantic compatibility proven; unresolved issue is packaging/import-graph cost and whether narrower surface is justified.
assessments.whyNotFirst: May be a no-op; lower expected frontier delta than G-AF3's generalization test.

assessments.closureRisk: High — externally blocked; not closable within current budget unit.
assessments.dominantCost: Waiting on external DeepSeek DNS recovery; cannot proceed now.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Retry no-tool incremental after DNS recovery; run replay/batch and resolved-provider controls.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Control-path repair already admitted in source; live experiments blocked on external DNS recovery.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Externally blocked on DNS recovery; cannot deliver value now.

assessments.closureRisk: Very high — dominant external admission blocker; not closable.
assessments.dominantCost: Procuring an independent Linux/systemd host that does not exist.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Obtain independent host; verify immutable deployment kit; provision separated signers.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Negative control; blocked on absence of independently administered Linux/systemd host.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Negative control, externally blocked, no host available; deferred.

result.choiceRationale: G-AF3 is the highest expected research value: it is the only candidate that would actually expand the empirical frontier (robustness/generalization across encounter variants) rather than close out or package already-complete work. It is also closable now — no external blocker. R-P5 is near-complete (mechanism selection done, only final gates/commit remain), so marginal research value of another unit is low; HOST-PKG is a packaging/import-graph audit that may be a no-op; H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery; F-C2 is a negative control blocked on an independently administered host that does not exist.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether G-AF3's encounter variants reveal that AF002 priors are fixed-encounter overfit (defect-discovery / prior-narrowing) versus surviving perturbations (prior-generalization).
result.selectionFalsifier: If G-AF3's variant construction turns out to be trivially degenerate (variants not materially different), or if R-P5's final portable/physical gates reveal a hidden mechanism defect that would have made R-P5 the higher-value closeout, then the ranking would flip.
